name: l09-run-source
title: Run, source or exec
spec: Table with How, What happens, Variables visible afterwards. Rows: ./script.sh | new child process | No ; source script.sh or . script.sh | current shell executes the commands | Yes (green highlight) ; exec ./script.sh | replaces the current shell | shell no longer exists ; bash -x script.sh | run with tracing | No. Commands in monospace. Note: a child cannot change its parent's environment.
alt: Running, sourcing and exec differ in whether the script's variables survive in your shell.
cap: Only sourcing leaves the script's variables in your current shell.

name: l09-args
title: The three argument loops
spec: Script called as: script 'abc 123' qwe. Three rows each showing loop and output: for a in "$@" gives [abc 123] [qwe] (green, correct); for a in $@ gives [abc] [123] [qwe] (orange, broken); for a in "$*" gives [abc 123 qwe] one word. Loops in monospace. Note: "$*" joins with the first character of IFS.
alt: Three ways of looping over arguments and what each one produces.
cap: Quoted dollar-at keeps each argument as one word, while the other forms split or join them.

name: l09-subshell
title: Subshell versus group
spec: Two panels. Left (commands ) subshell: child copy of the shell, example myvar=10 then ( myvar=20 ); echo gives 10, changes vanish. Right { commands; } current shell: myvar=30 then echo gives 30; note the spaces and semicolon; use for one redirection: { echo a; echo b; } > file. Footer orange: each stage of a pipeline runs in its own subshell, so echo hi | read x; echo "$x" prints nothing. Code in monospace.
alt: A subshell discards its changes, while a brace group runs in the current shell.
cap: Changes made inside a subshell vanish when it ends, but a brace group changes the current shell.

name: l09-retry
title: Retry with backoff
spec: Loop diagram: run command; success then done; failure then 'attempts left?' If no, 'failed after n attempts' exit 1 (orange). If yes, sleep delay then delay doubles, back to run. Side box monospace: retry 5 2 curl -fsS https://example.com/file -o /tmp/file ; timeout 30 ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 -o BatchMode=yes node01 true. Green bar: always put a timeout on anything that can block.
alt: A retry loop that sleeps with a doubling delay until the attempts run out.
cap: Retries with a growing delay and a timeout keep scripts from hanging or failing on transient errors.
